title: On the Poetics of Adversarial Prompts: Why Bad Verse Works and Good Verse Works Better — A Literary Analysis of Bisconti et al. (2025) and the Future of Semantic Security (Revised Standalone Edition, v2.0)
creator: Nobel Glas; Talos Morrow; Johannes Sigil
description:
A revised standalone v2.0 scholarly paper by Nobel Glas, Talos Morrow, and Johannes Sigil. It critically reads Bisconti et al.’s 2025 study of poetic formatting and LLM guardrail bypass, arguing that the tested prompts display **surface-form poeticization** rather than fully generative poetic transformation.

The paper proposes **adversarial poetry** as high-density poetic language whose categorical ambiguity challenges binary threat classification, and it connects this claim to crystalline semiosis and a future Measurement of Meaning program. Its prediction that bypass efficacy rises with semantic density is explicitly a hypothesis; the paper does not report the controlled experiment needed to validate it. Version 2 corrects defects in the December 2025 appendix state and grants the theory a standalone scholarly manifestation without withdrawing the earlier artistic context.
